stories.title: Managing holiday stress through intention
stories.summary: Thanksgiving gatherings often bring pressure and complicated dynamics. Dr. Alice Conners-Kellgren of Tufts Medical Center suggests abandoning the pursuit of perfection, which she describes as an elusive goal. Instead, she recommends setting a clear intention for the day to help manage expectations and reduce potential anxiety.

stories.title: Riley Children’s Health opens specialized pediatric unit
stories.summary: Riley Children’s Health has opened a new 11-bed inpatient unit in Indianapolis for children with complex medical and behavioral health needs. The facility is expected to serve approximately 325 patients annually. David Biggerstaff, president of Riley Children’s Health, called the unit an innovative approach to compassionate care.

stories.title: Experts address holiday loneliness and stress
stories.summary: Mental health experts report that the holiday season frequently triggers loneliness, grief, and family stress. Many individuals experience post-holiday disappointment after failing to meet the expectations set by social media and commercials. Professionals suggest that comparing one's reality to curated holiday imagery often exacerbates these feelings.

stories.title: AI tools show mixed results for healthcare workers
stories.summary: A review of 27 studies published between 2015 and 2025 indicates that AI deployment in healthcare provides inconsistent occupational benefits. Researchers evaluated outcomes including stress, burnout, and job satisfaction. The findings suggest that AI tools do not deliver uniform wellbeing improvements across real-world clinical environments.

stories.title: Holiday stress impacts mental health
stories.summary: Nearly nine in 10 U.S. adults report feeling stressed during the holidays, with over 60% of those living with mental illness reporting worsened symptoms. Washtenaw County Health Department spokesperson Beth Ann Hamilton notes that personal and professional demands, including academic finals, often peak during this period.

stories.title: Shelby County introduces jail advocacy phone line
stories.summary: The Shelby County Sheriff’s Office has launched a phone line for families to report medical and mental health concerns regarding incarcerated relatives. Sheriff Anthony Buckner stated the initiative aims to bridge communication gaps. The service is intended to ensure that family concerns are heard by the department.

stories.title: Study examines school mental health program implementation
stories.summary: Research published in Administration and Policy in Mental Health indicates that while adolescent prevention programs often succeed in clinical trials, few achieve widespread implementation. The study evaluated 181 intervention trials to determine why evidence-based programs frequently falter after the conclusion of experimental funding.

stories.title: Catholic leaders to host mental health summit
stories.summary: Bishop John Dolan and Deacon Ed Shoener will headline the inaugural Catholic Counseling and Mental Health Ministry Summit in Phoenix this February. The event aims to address suicide prevention and pastoral care. The summit will gather clergy, educators, and mental health professionals to discuss church responses to illness.

stories.title: Youth turning to AI for mental health support
stories.summary: Roughly one in five Canadian youth are using AI chatbots for emotional support, according to UBC neuroscientist Dr. Julie Robillard. While these tools simulate supportive human conversation, experts are encouraging parents to help young users navigate these digital spaces safely as AI integration into wellbeing continues to grow.

stories.title: Relaxation exercises compared to loving-kindness meditation
stories.summary: A 2026 study in PLOS One compared the effects of loving-kindness meditation against simple muscle relaxation exercises in 69 adults. The research examined whether focusing on compassion offers greater benefits for pain and social well-being than basic relaxation techniques, which are also used to manage physical discomfort.

stories.title: Mindfulness program shows clinical improvements
stories.summary: A retrospective evaluation of the Mindful Mental Health Service at Cambridge Health Alliance reports a 72 percent completion rate among 1,796 enrollments. The study suggests that a trauma-informed, insurance-reimbursable mindfulness program can achieve meaningful clinical improvements within a public safety-net healthcare setting.

stories.title: Mindfulness linked to social media habits
stories.summary: A review published in PLOS One suggests that mindfulness is associated with better mental health and more beneficial social media use. With average daily usage reaching 2.3 hours, researchers are investigating how mindfulness might mitigate the potential negative effects of technology on the mental health of young adults.

stories.title: Edmonton community hosts wellness brunch
stories.summary: Over 60 women attended the Women’s Wellness Brunch at Beth Israel Synagogue in Edmonton on October 18. The event, which featured meaningful learning and a menu including egg and potato kugel, was organized to support the local Mikvah. The turnout exceeded initial expectations of thirty attendees.

stories.title: Mindfulness training may increase workplace hostility
stories.summary: A month-long experiment found that mindfulness training can lead to increased anger and contempt among employees who already distrust others. While companies often offer these programs to reduce stress, some participants reported higher levels of rudeness toward coworkers following the training sessions.

stories.title: Monk advocates for inner cultivation in AI era
stories.summary: Ven. Ilmuk, a former mathematics doctoral student, has published a guide to Buddhist breathing meditation. He argues that inner cultivation and metacognition will become increasingly important as AI technology advances. He also suggests that Buddhism must emphasize its unique strengths to address declining interest in the tradition.

stories.title: Former executive launches meditation program for leaders
stories.summary: Susan Chen, a former Wall Street executive, has launched the Superlative Method to provide Vedic meditation for high-performing professionals. The program is designed for executives experiencing stress-related health issues. Chen states the curriculum is based on her own experiences managing risk at firms like Morgan Stanley.

stories.title: Meditation approach focuses on side-by-side gratitude
stories.summary: Mindfulness teacher Shamash Alidina suggests that gratitude practices should not require feeling thankful on cue. His approach encourages individuals to acknowledge their current difficulties while holding one small, ordinary appreciation alongside them. The method aims to connect gratitude to personal values rather than forced emotional states.

stories.title: Mindfulness teacher addresses gratitude fatigue
stories.summary: Mindfulness teacher Shamash Alidina notes that holiday-season advice to focus on the positive can feel dismissive to those struggling with hardship. He suggests that being told to feel grateful when life is difficult can make individuals feel as though they are failing to appreciate their lives properly.

stories.title: Sleep consistency may influence memory formation
stories.summary: A study in the Journal of Sleep Research suggests that sleep consistency affects how the brain forms and stores memories. Researchers examined whether changing sleep duration from night to night impacts memory differently than consistent rest. The findings challenge the idea that weekend catch-up sleep compensates for lost time.

stories.title: Study warns of medication risks for older adults
stories.summary: Research from the University at Buffalo indicates that nearly one in three older adults with cognitive disorders remains on medications linked to impaired memory, balance, and thinking. The study highlights safety concerns for aging populations, particularly those living with dementia, as these prescriptions continue to be used.

stories.title: Artificially sweetened drinks linked to shorter sleep
stories.summary: A study of over 10,000 South Korean adults published in Nutrients found that consuming artificially sweetened carbonated beverages correlates with shorter sleep duration and depressive symptoms. Conversely, the analysis identified that sugar-sweetened soft drinks were associated with longer sleep periods among the participants surveyed.

stories.title: Autism and the search for effective insomnia treatments
stories.summary: Adults with autism spectrum disorder experience sleep difficulties at rates between 54% and 90%. These issues, including insomnia and circadian rhythm disorders, are linked to reduced physical and mental health. Researchers are currently investigating whether cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia can effectively address these persistent sleep challenges.

stories.title: Yoga ranked as superior exercise for sleep quality
stories.summary: An analysis of 30 clinical trials published in Sleep and Biological Rhythms identified yoga as the most effective exercise for improving sleep quality. Researchers favored high-intensity sessions lasting under 30 minutes, practiced twice weekly. The review compared seven different forms of physical activity to determine sleep benefits.

stories.title: Prescriptions for potentially harmful sleep drugs persist
stories.summary: A University at Buffalo study in the Journal of the American Geriatrics Society reports that about one in three older adults with cognitive disorders is still exposed to medications that can worsen memory and balance. While usage declined since 2011, researchers suggest current prescription rates remain too high.

stories.title: Bedtime planning linked to better rest
stories.summary: A study of 119 university students published in Sleep found that creating a bedtime plan is associated with earlier sleep and increased rest. Psychologists define the tendency to delay sleep without reason as bedtime procrastination, suggesting that simple scheduling may help mitigate the habit of late-night scrolling.

stories.title: Simba mattress sale follows consumer reports
stories.summary: Mattress specialist Simba is offering a Black Friday discount of up to 33% on its products. The company markets its mattresses as a solution for insomnia, citing customer testimonials that claim the equipment transformed their sleep patterns. The retailer notes that poor sleep may stem from outdated bedding.

stories.title: Pillow marketed as insomnia solution
stories.summary: Simba is promoting its pillows as a remedy for mild insomnia, featuring testimonials from customers who report feeling more rested. The company suggests that interrupted sleep can be addressed by investing in new equipment, and is currently offering sales on its sleep products to potential buyers.

stories.title: Park district promotes winter walking for health
stories.summary: The Johnny Appleseed Park District in Ohio continues its weekly walking program through the winter months. Officials emphasize the mental and physical health benefits of the sessions, noting that outdoor activity helps participants maintain fitness and wellbeing even as temperatures drop and seasonal motivation potentially declines.

stories.title: Exercise shows benefits for COPD patients
stories.summary: A multicentre study led by Lund University found that exercise leads to measurable improvements in the small airways of patients with COPD. These changes are often not detected by standard lung function tests. The findings suggest physical activity provides benefits beyond those captured by traditional clinical assessments.

stories.title: Lisa Faulkner favors low-pressure fitness routine
stories.summary: Actor Lisa Faulkner maintains her health through daily walks and yoga rather than intensive gym workouts. Faulkner stated that she prefers sustainable movement over high-intensity training, aiming for a healthy body that functions well. Her routine avoids the pressure of conventional fitness standards in favor of lifestyle integration.

stories.title: Walking cited as effective cross-training for runners
stories.summary: Walking is described as a natural activity that improves aerobic fitness, bone density, and mental wellbeing. Research from The Ramblers indicates that 68% of people use green spaces for walking to boost their mood, while other studies suggest that mindful walking can provide additional cognitive benefits.

stories.title: Study examines exercise order for blood sugar control
stories.summary: A study published in iScience investigated whether the sequence of aerobic and resistance training affects blood sugar levels in people with type 2 diabetes. Researchers are evaluating how exercise intensity and order influence insulin sensitivity to provide clearer guidance for managing glucose through physical activity.

stories.title: Heart surgeon discusses blood pressure exercise
stories.summary: A heart surgeon has identified a specific exercise for blood pressure management that requires no equipment and can be performed at home. The doctor notes that high blood pressure, often called the silent killer, increases the risk of stroke and dementia, necessitating regular, effective physical activity.

stories.title: Olympian recommends rowing for full-body strength
stories.summary: Olympic gold medalist Alex Gregory advocates for rowing machines as a complete workout for aerobic endurance and muscular strength. Gregory, who uses rowing as the cornerstone of his own fitness regimen, suggests the machine is suitable for beginners because it engages the entire body rather than just legs.

stories.title: Michelle Yeoh maintains strength with tai chi
stories.summary: Global megastar Michelle Yeoh, 64, incorporates core exercises and daily tai chi into her routine to maintain strength. Despite her physically demanding on-screen roles, Yeoh emphasizes a disciplined approach to movement that supports her wellbeing and presence, focusing on consistent practice to prepare for future projects.

stories.title: Tess Daly shares varied fitness routine
stories.summary: Television presenter Tess Daly, 57, maintains her fitness through a combination of dancing, short trampoline sessions, and strength exercises. According to Women's Health, her routine avoids conventional gym workouts in favor of spontaneous movement and short sessions throughout the day, supplemented by yoga, stretching, and meditation.

stories.title: Hemp seeds in yogurt
stories.summary: Researchers at the Agricultural Technological Institute of Castilla y León found that adding enzymatically treated hemp seeds to yogurt increases antioxidant activity by up to 11-fold and inhibits a blood pressure-related enzyme. The study, published in Molecules, tested concentrations of 2%, 4% and 6% in dairy yogurt.

stories.title: Gut bacteria and weight regain
stories.summary: A narrative review in Nutrients examines how anti-obesity drugs like semaglutide alter gut microbiota and whether these shifts influence weight maintenance after treatment. While these medications improve weight-loss outcomes, the review investigates why maintaining those results remains difficult for many of the 890 million adults living with obesity.

stories.title: Microbiome and blood sugar
stories.summary: New research from The Ohio State University suggests that gut microbes influence how individuals respond to dietary changes. A clinical trial in adults with prediabetes indicates that blood sugar control may be affected by both the initial microbiome composition and how it shifts in response to whole grains.

As a lifestyle journalist, she crafts compelling, relatable narratives across diverse touchpoints of the human experience, including wellness, mental health, relationships, interior design, home decor, food, travel, and fashion that gently nudge readers toward living a little better. stories.title: Salty snacks and gut health
stories.summary: An observational study of over 111,000 children and adolescents links high consumption of salty snacks to a 32% higher risk of inflammatory bowel disease by young adulthood. The study also associated childhood fruit and fish intake with lower Crohn’s disease risk, though researchers noted these are observational links.

stories.title: Iron supplements for children
stories.summary: A Cochrane review of 114 studies involving 50,000 participants found that daily iron tablets reduce the risk of iron deficiency anaemia in children and adolescents. The review reported little to no effect on other common illnesses, confirming iron supplementation as a standard preventative measure for the condition.

stories.title: Exercise versus diet for longevity
stories.summary: A review in Mayo Clinic Proceedings suggests that regular physical activity and cardiorespiratory fitness have a stronger association with reduced mortality risk than dietary quality. Researchers Glenn Gaesser and Robert Sallis argue that while eating habits remain important, movement provides larger reductions in the risk of death.

stories.title: Exercise Shows Stronger Link to Longevity Than Diet
stories.summary: Regular physical activity and strong cardiorespiratory fitness have a greater association with reduced mortality risk than diet quality alone, according to a review of dozens of scientific studies published in Mayo Clinic Proceedings. Researchers Glenn Gaesser of Arizona State University and Robert Sallis of Kaiser Permanente Medical Center examined how

stories.summary: A newly published long-term investigation into wild Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins demonstrates that an individual’s social grouping patterns become progressively more predictable across its lifespan, with the most pronounced behavioural consistency emerging among the longest-lived animals. The findings, highlighted in a PLOS Biology Primer by Erin R. Siracusa examining research by

stories.title: Dolphin social consistency and longevity
stories.summary: A 40-year study of 400 wild Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins in Western Australia found that individuals with consistent social grouping patterns tended to live longer. The findings suggest that for dolphins, the stability of social life is a key factor in survival within their natural communities.

stories.title: Why Longevity Experts Are Talking About Sleep
stories.summary: By Elizabeth Hamilton for Sleeping.com Interest in healthy aging is reaching beyond the doctor’s office. McKinsey’s 2025 consumer research reports growing demand for longevity products and services. Nutrition, exercise, strength training and stress management are familiar starting points. stories.title: Red meat avoidance and health
stories.summary: A working paper from Harvard researchers reports that patients with alpha-gal syndrome who stopped eating red meat experienced modest cardiometabolic health benefits. The paper, circulated by the National Bureau of Economic Research, has not yet been peer-reviewed and challenges current federal dietary guidelines regarding animal-based proteins.

stories.title: Rediscovering Holistic Healing: Vaidya Ashok on Ayurveda, Su Jok and the Art of Integrative Healthcare
stories.summary: Charu Bhatia, Senior News Editor, Business Remedies, in conversation with Vaidya Ashok of Sai Sahara Hospital and Research Centre, Jaipur Ayurveda, India’s ancient system of holistic healthcare, emphasises the importance of balance between the body, mind and overall well-being. stories.title: Plans afoot to set up 5 new homeopathic, ayurvedic medical colleges in Odisha: Health Minister - Sambad English
stories.summary: Bhubaneswar: The state government will take the necessary steps to establish five new homeopathic and ayurvedic medical colleges in Odisha, health and Family Welfare Minister Mukesh Mahaling said on Wednesday. According to the minister, the state government has proposed to establish the five new homeopathic and Ayurvedic medical in the

stories.title: Ayurveda wellness retreats
stories.summary: India’s traditional Ayurvedic treatments are drawing international visitors to wellness retreats promising holistic health. These centers combine herbal treatments, massage and yoga to restore what practitioners describe as the body’s natural balance, despite limited scientific evidence supporting the effectiveness of these specific regimes.

stories.title: Health minister calls for Ayurveda Council Act amendments
stories.summary: Health and Food Sanitation Minister Nisha Mehta has called for amendments to the Ayurveda Council Act to ensure representation and professional respect for all alternative medicine disciplines. The minister met with stakeholders on Wednesday to discuss addressing existing problems within the sector through legislative changes.

stories.title: Parul University receives grant for sickle cell pain research
stories.summary: Parul University has received a 1.04 crore rupee grant from the Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences to study Ayurvedic interventions for sickle cell pain. The research will focus on adolescents in tribal communities in Gujarat. The study aims to determine if traditional methods provide relief.

stories.title: Nationwide activities mark 11th Ayurveda Day
stories.summary: The 11th Ayurveda Day 2026 featured nationwide outreach, including yoga camps, webinars, and a Run for Ayurveda. Institutions like the Central Ayurveda Research Institute organized events to engage the public and students on healthy lifestyles. The day concluded with various academic and community wellness competitions.
